name: MonarchSkipLink
title: SkipLink
summary: An action that moves focus past repeated navigation to the main content of a screen, for keyboard, switch access and TalkBack users, with Modifier.monarchSkipLinkTarget for the element it moves to.
whenToUse: At the top of a screen whose navigation (a long toolbar, a row of filters, a rail of links) comes before the main content in the focus order.
whenNotToUse: On screens where the content comes first or the navigation is a bottom bar; TalkBack users already move by heading there.
api: @Composable fun MonarchSkipLink(target: FocusRequester, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, label: String? = null, onSkip: (() -> Unit)? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

options.name: target
options.description: The requester of the main content, shared with Modifier.monarchSkipLinkTarget.

options.name: label
options.description: The label. null uses "Skip to main content".

options.name: onSkip
options.description: Called after focus moved, for example to scroll the content into view.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the press and focus interactions.

states.name: activated
states.description: Focus moves to the element marked with monarchSkipLinkTarget.

appearance: A small secondary MonarchButton: the surface with the default border and the default text. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web SkipLink is hidden until it receives keyboard focus and jumps to an element id. Android has no hidden focus-only element that TalkBack also reaches, so the skip link is a visible small button, read first in its traversal group (traversalIndex -1), and it moves input focus to a FocusRequester instead of an id.
accessibility: It is a button with a touch target of at least 48dp, named "Skip to main content" or the label.
It is read before the other elements of its traversal group.
Activating it requests focus on the target, which monarchSkipLinkTarget makes focusable; the next key press or swipe continues from there.
edgeCases: A target that is not in the composition is not focused; requestFocus has no effect.
Whether TalkBack's accessibility focus follows the input focus was not tried on a device.
